# The note lists songs in the format: "- <Song Name> BY <Artist(s)> RELEASED_AT <Month/Year or TODO>"
# The first four songs have release months, the rest have "RELEASED_AT TODO".
# Let's extract the songs with "RELEASED_AT TODO" and their artists, so we can look up their release months.
import re

note_content = note_details["content"]
todo_pattern = r"- (.*?) BY (.*?) RELEASED_AT TODO"
todo_songs = re.findall(todo_pattern, note_content)
print(todo_songs)  # List of (song, artists) tuples needing release month info

# Now we have the release month/year for all songs with "RELEASED_AT TODO".
# Let's update the note content by replacing each "RELEASED_AT TODO" with the correct month/year.
# We'll build a mapping and update the note content accordingly.

todo_release_info = [
    ("Lost in the Embrace of Night", "Noah Bennett", "03/2021"),
    ("Lonely Skies", "Aria Sterling", "11/2022"),
    ("Caught in a Web of Lies", "Hazel Winter, Ava Morgan", "03/2021"),
    ("On the Border of Reality", "Lily Moon, Zoey James", "08/2022"),
    ("A Love That Never Was", "Mia Sullivan, Carter Knight", "10/2020"),
    ("Astral Serenity", "Orion Steele", "12/2019"),
    ("Between Reality and Reverie", "Aria Sterling", "03/2020"),
    ("Strangers Again", "Oceanic Odyssey", "06/2022"),
    ("The Mirage of a Perfect Life", "Soulful Reverie", "11/2020"),
    ("Wilted Roses on the Vine", "Velvet Echo", "02/2020"),
    ("When All Words Fail Us", "Marcus Lane", "07/2020"),
    ("Final Echo", "Hazel Winter", "07/2022"),
]

updated_content = note_content
for song, artists, month_year in todo_release_info:
    # Build the exact line to replace
    pattern = f"- {song} BY {artists} RELEASED_AT TODO"
    replacement = f"- {song} BY {artists} RELEASED_AT {month_year}"
    updated_content = updated_content.replace(pattern, replacement)

# Now, update the note with the new content.

)
